waterbody.localityResolution: The abstract says water-quality assessment used six sites around the dam and reports fish collected and analyzed in the AWFR; it does not name the sites, give coordinates, or define the relationship between each fish sample and site.

decision: Retain as a discovery lead for Angat freshwater food-web research. Do not publish a species-specific diet, current occurrence, native/invasive classification, abundance, fishing recommendation, or management conclusion from this abstract.

source.title: Diet analysis and risk screening of native and introduced fish species in Angat Watershed Forest Reserve: Implications on protection and management
source.conference: 6th Biannual Conference of the Asian Society for Hydrobiology, Seoul, 1–4 July 2024
source.access: The official ASH catalog lists the 2024 abstract book. The abstract text was inspected through a search-indexed copy hosted by a third party; direct opening timed out. UST independently confirms the presentation and award, not its scientific results.

abstractReportedEvidence.sampling: Water-quality assessment at six sites around the dam; the abstract says fish were collected and analyzed but gives no sampling dates, site names, capture coordinates, specimen identifiers, vouchers, or sample sizes.
abstractReportedEvidence.dietSummary: The abstract says fish material and Chironomus sp. were dominant prey categories across all five fishes using frequency, numerical composition, and index-of-relative-importance summaries. It provides no taxon-specific values, prey species, life stage, body-size, seasonal, or site breakdown.
abstractReportedEvidence.riskScreeningSummary: The authors report that all four introduced species scored high risk in both basic and climate-change AS-ISK screening. The abstract provides no scores, completed questionnaire, assessor details, or validation materials.

reuse.basis: The ASH catalog page carries a site-level all-rights-reserved notice; no item-specific license or permission for reuse of the abstract book or data was verified.
reuse.disposition: Keep bibliographic metadata and short attributed research notes in the private source ledger. Do not copy the abstract, reproduce its figures/tables, or distribute the book.

limitations: Conference abstract only; not a complete paper or a peer-reviewed article record verified in this review.
The six named sampling sites, fish collection dates, sample sizes, vouchers, and fish-to-site crosswalk are unavailable.
The broad diet categories do not establish a usable prey list for any individual fish species and are not bait guidance.
Author-reported endemicity and AS-ISK scores are not independently verified legal, conservation, or invasion-status decisions.
A presentation confirmation from UST verifies the work was presented, not the underlying methods or results.
nextStep: Look for an author- or institution-hosted full paper/poster or supplementary data with dated fish-to-site and stomach-content rows, voucher/specimen crosswalks, and explicit reuse terms. Keep Angat and Pantabangan as distinct waterbodies and the L3 baseline incomplete.
